categories.name: Accounting & finance
categories.blurb: The ledger. This is the one the dashboard cannot do without: revenue, cost, balances, budget.

categories.name: System of record
categories.blurb: The software your industry runs on. It supplies the unit of work behind every financial figure.

categories.name: Project & field management
categories.blurb: Schedules, change orders, field reports, the cost that has not reached the ledger yet.

categories.name: Task & work management
categories.blurb: What each person owes this week. Feeds the home page and the role views.

categories.name: Inventory & operations
categories.blurb: Stock, throughput, equipment, utilization. Turns a cost line into a cost per unit.

categories.name: CRM, marketing & pipeline
categories.blurb: What is coming. Pipeline never enters a financial statement, it sits beside it.

categories.name: HR & payroll
categories.blurb: Headcount, labor cost, who holds which role. Drives the view levels.

categories.name: Document storage
categories.blurb: Where the contracts, statements and reports live, so a figure links to its paperwork.

categories.name: Communication
categories.blurb: Mail, chat, calendar. The dashboard delivers to where people already are.

connectors.name: Sage Intacct
connectors.auth: Web Services sender ID + company user
connectors.note: Running live. Reads trial balance, GL detail, per-company close dates and balances by location. The deepest adapter we have.

connectors.name: QuickBooks Online
connectors.note: Running live on a real company file, including journaled postings and class/location tracking. The right ledger for most companies under about $50M.

connectors.name: Oracle NetSuite
connectors.note: Full ERP. SuiteQL gives real query power, and saved searches are the pragmatic route for anything heavy.

connectors.name: Xero
connectors.note: Clean API, generous reporting endpoints. Strong second choice to QuickBooks.

connectors.name: Puzzle
connectors.note: Accounting built for startups, sits on top of the bank and card feeds. Good fit where the books are young.

connectors.name: Sage 100 Contractor
connectors.note: On-premise. Usually read through a scheduled export rather than an API.

connectors.name: Trimble Viewpoint Vista
connectors.note: Construction ERP. Job cost and WIP land natively, which shortens the work considerably.

connectors.name: Foundation Software
connectors.note: Payroll-heavy construction accounting, common in the trades.

connectors.name: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central
connectors.note: Where a company is already on Microsoft, this keeps one identity provider for the whole stack.

connectors.name: Stripe
connectors.note: Billing truth for subscription businesses: MRR, churn and failed payments before they reach the ledger.

connectors.name: Ramp
connectors.note: Card and spend data at transaction level, days before the statement closes.

connectors.name: BILL (Bill.com)
connectors.note: AP approvals. Useful for an accurate payables ageing ahead of the ledger.

connectors.name: Plaid
connectors.note: Bank balances and transactions direct, for a cash figure that does not wait on a reconciliation.

connectors.name: Restaurant365
connectors.note: Accounting built for multi-unit restaurants, with inventory and recipe costing beside the ledger, so food cost ties to the books.

connectors.name: Procore
connectors.note: Running live. Projects, budgets, change events and commitments. Rate limited to roughly one pull an hour per app, so build webhook-driven, never polling.

connectors.name: Autodesk Construction Cloud
connectors.note: Strong on design documents and issues. Cost Management is a separate scope.

connectors.name: Buildertrend
connectors.note: Residential builder workflow. API access sits on the higher plans.

connectors.name: Fieldwire
connectors.note: Field task and punch lists, light and quick to wire.

connectors.name: Bluebeam
connectors.note: Markups carry a cost column, which is where a change order is first priced. Procore is the hub the two meet in.

connectors.name: Smartsheet
connectors.note: Where a company's schedule is really a grid. Reads cleanly, writes back too.

connectors.name: Jira
connectors.note: For an engineering organization this is the system of record for delivery, and JQL makes the queries honest.

connectors.name: Microsoft Project for the web
connectors.note: Reaches through Dataverse rather than Graph alone for anything beyond tasks.

connectors.name: monday.com
connectors.note: Running live across several boards. Send API-Version 2026-07 on every call: the silent default is older and missing half the mutations.

connectors.name: Asana
connectors.note: Portfolios and goals map well onto a role view.

connectors.name: ClickUp
connectors.note: Deep hierarchy, so decide early which level a dashboard row means.

connectors.name: Microsoft Planner & To Do
connectors.note: Running live. The right answer whenever a company is already on Microsoft 365, because it needs no new license.

connectors.name: Motion
connectors.note: Schedules the work itself. Reads as tasks with a planned block, which makes a capacity view possible.

connectors.name: Linear
connectors.note: Cycle and project data are first class, so delivery pace needs no reconstruction.

connectors.name: Notion
connectors.note: Database pages read fine. Pagination is unavoidable on anything large.

connectors.name: Trello
connectors.note: Simple and fast to wire where a board is really a pipeline.

connectors.name: SharePoint & OneDrive
connectors.note: Running live, including per-person trimmed document indexes. SharePoint REST accepts app-only tokens only when they are issued for a certificate, never a client secret.

connectors.name: Google Drive
connectors.note: Shared drives plus a service account give clean unattended reads.

connectors.name: Dropbox Business
connectors.note: Team folders and file events are both available, so an index can stay current.

connectors.name: Box
connectors.note: Metadata templates are unusually good, which helps a naming convention stick.

connectors.name: Egnyte
connectors.note: Common where a company wants on-premise and cloud at once.

connectors.name: ShareFile
connectors.note: Usually the system being migrated away from rather than the destination.

connectors.name: Microsoft Teams
connectors.note: Running live for reads. Where a company already runs Teams, nothing new has to be bought or learned.

connectors.name: Outlook mail & calendar
connectors.note: Running live. The calendar is the only honest source of where a day actually went.

connectors.name: Slack
connectors.note: Delivery as well as reading: a close or a variance can land in a channel the moment it is known.

connectors.name: Gmail & Google Calendar
connectors.note: Domain-wide delegation makes unattended reads possible without a password anywhere.

connectors.name: Twilio
connectors.note: For the people who never open a dashboard: a text when a number crosses a line.

connectors.name: Zoom
connectors.note: Meeting and recording metadata, useful where a board pack cites a meeting.

connectors.name: ADP Workforce Now
connectors.note: Adapter built and tested against fixtures. Certificate issuance is the slow part, measured in weeks not hours.

connectors.name: Gusto
connectors.note: Clean payroll API, quick to wire, good fit under about 200 people.

connectors.name: Rippling
connectors.note: Carries HR, payroll and device management, so one grant answers several questions.

connectors.name: Paylocity
connectors.note: Common in the trades. Labor cost by job is the figure worth pulling.

connectors.name: BambooHR
connectors.note: Headcount and the org chart, which is what the view levels are built from.

connectors.name: Workday
connectors.note: Enterprise. A custom RaaS report is usually faster than the REST surface.

connectors.name: 7shifts
connectors.note: Restaurant scheduling and time clock. Labor hours by location, which is what sales per labor hour is divided by.

connectors.name: Salesforce
connectors.note: Where pipeline already lives, SOQL makes a weighted forecast straightforward.

connectors.name: HubSpot
connectors.note: The pragmatic choice for a company with no CRM: free to start and the API is complete.

connectors.name: monday CRM
connectors.note: Running live across four company boards feeding one executive board. A pursuit is never a fact, so it is excluded from every statement by construction.

connectors.name: Google Ads
connectors.note: Spend, clicks and conversions by campaign. Spend is the figure the marketing page totals, so it never needs typing in.

connectors.name: Meta Ads
connectors.note: Facebook and Instagram spend and lead forms by campaign, joined to the CRM by the lead's own id.

connectors.name: Google Analytics
connectors.note: Website visits and inquiry forms by source, which is how organic and referral traffic gets counted at all.

connectors.name: Pipedrive
connectors.note: Light and stage-driven, quick to read.

connectors.name: Shopify
connectors.note: Orders, SKUs, locations and margin per item. The GraphQL Admin API is the only route with a future.

connectors.name: Square
connectors.note: Strong for a physical footprint: sales per hour, per location, per employee.

connectors.name: Lightspeed Retail
connectors.note: Good inventory depth for multi-store retail.

connectors.name: Toast
connectors.note: The restaurant point of sale. Checks, covers, labor and food cost against sales, by location and daypart.

connectors.name: PowerSchool SIS
connectors.note: Enrolment and attendance, which is what the funding figure is actually built from.

connectors.name: Infinite Campus
connectors.note: OneRoster is the portable route and worth preferring where both exist.

connectors.name: Skyward
connectors.note: Finance and SIS in one, so a per-student cost needs no join across vendors.

connectors.name: Blackbaud
connectors.note: Independent schools: tuition, giving and financial aid in one place.

connectors.name: athenahealth
connectors.note: Appointments, encounters and claims. Visits, no-shows and days in A/R all come from here, so nobody keys them in.

connectors.name: NextGen Healthcare
connectors.note: Common in multi-specialty groups. Practice management and billing read the same way.

connectors.name: Rockwell Plex
connectors.note: Cloud MES. Production, scrap and OEE arrive without a historian in between.

connectors.name: Epicor Kinetic
connectors.note: Manufacturing ERP. Job cost is native, which is most of the work already done.

connectors.name: Katana
connectors.note: Light manufacturing. Quick to wire and sensible for a smaller plant.

connectors.name: Tulip
connectors.note: Operator-level data from the line itself, which is where a throughput claim is settled.

connectors.name: McLeod PowerBroker / LoadMaster
connectors.note: The TMS most asset carriers run. Loads, lanes and settlements.

connectors.name: Trimble TMW
connectors.note: Enterprise TMS. Pairs with their telematics for a cost per mile that ties.

connectors.name: Samsara
connectors.note: Telematics, hours of service and fuel. The cleanest API in the fleet world.

connectors.name: Motive
connectors.note: ELD and fuel, strong on driver-level data for a cost per mile.

connectors.name: project44
connectors.note: Visibility across carriers you do not own. On-time performance without asking anyone.

connectors.name: Stripe Billing
connectors.note: Subscriptions, MRR movement and churn. For a SaaS company this is the system of record, not the ledger.

connectors.name: Fishbowl Inventory
connectors.note: QuickBooks-adjacent warehouse management, common where the ledger is QBO.

connectors.name: Cin7
connectors.note: Multi-channel stock. Landed cost is available, which margin work needs.

connectors.name: NetSuite WMS
connectors.note: Only sensible where NetSuite is already the ledger.

connectors.name: Fleetio
connectors.note: Maintenance cost per asset, which is the line that quietly decides a fleet's margin.

connectors.name: Zoho Inventory
connectors.note: Inexpensive and complete enough for a single warehouse.

connectors.name: Odoo
connectors.note: Open source, so the whole model is readable. Self-hosted instances vary a great deal.
